channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport, killing at least five
item.description: At least five people were killed and five injured after an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday and crashed into several vehicles, officials said. Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said there was “no apparent threat to public safety” following the crash.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: "Ready to talk": German far-right celebrates victory
item.description: “Everything is possible” is the election campaign slogan of the far-right Alternative for Germany, the leader in Saxony-Anhalt, where the polls have just closed. It talks of a seminal moment for the country. Ulrich Siegmund, who has been polling in pole position to become the state leader, knows he has history in his grasp.
item.dc:creator: Gavin LEE

item.title: 🔴Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
item.description: Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party headed towards a landslide victory in state ​elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, with 44.5 percent of the vote, early results showed. But despite the scale of its projected win, it was not immediately clear whether AfD would be able to form Germany’s first far-right state government since World War II.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: AfD could lead "the first far-right state government since the dark days of Nazism"
item.description: Voting is underway in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. "If the AfD does form a government in Saxony-Anhalt, that would make it the first regional government headed by a far-right party since the end of the Second World War, since the dark days of Nazism", our correspondent Nick Holdsworth explains.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Deauville Film Festival: What’s your favourite American film?
item.description: The United States ranks second in the world in terms of the number of films produced. It produces between 500 and 700 films every year, which is just behind India. The Deauville Film Festival, with its stars, premieres and awards, aims to showcase the very best of what’s being made across the Atlantic. But on the other side of the screen, moviegoers also have their say. What’s your favourite American film? Is it one that shaped your childhood, or a recent discovery? Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca hit the streets of Deauville to ask that very question.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: What could change in Saxony-Anhalt if the AfD wins?
item.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. Recent surveys place the AfD at just over 40%, followed by Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) at 23%. If the AfD wins, "one of the main things they want to change is the education system. They say they want to reset education," our journalist Shirli Stibon explains.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Under-fire FIFA boss Infantino to seek re-election despite calls to resign
item.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino plans to seek his fourth and final term in next year’s election, despite the outrage sparked by his now-shelved plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. “Nothing has changed,” a spokesman for football’s governing body confirmed on Sunday, referring to an announcement Infantino made back in April.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The week in pictures: Nepal rescue operations, World Nomad Games and Russian strikes on Kyiv
item.description: From the desperate search for workers trapped in the hydropower tunnels buried by the catastrophic flooding in Nepal to crowds of women mourning the victims of a US bombardment of a wedding in southern Iran, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Germany: AfD's Ulrich Siegmund eyes outright majority
item.description: Under its 35-year-old lead ​candidate Ulrich Siegmund, the ‌AfD has polled above 40% for months and has a realistic shot at winning an absolute majority if several smaller parties fail ⁠to clear Germany's 5% hurdle to enter parliament.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ukraine-Russia talks: What are the US objectives?
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace, more than 4½ years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. We discuss this topic with our guest, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center at the Atlantic Council.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Egyptian TV presenter Sarah Khalifa sentenced to death in drug case
item.description: Sarah Khalifa, a well-known Egyptian TV presenter, has been sentenced to death for her involvement in a drug ring, state media reported over the weekend. Eleven others were also convicted in the case and handed a death sentence. Khalifa is best known for her program “Mission Impossible”.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: AI: The future of smart households?
item.description: Could artificial intelligence soon be running our households? Beyond our smartphones, AI is now powering everything from fridges to lawnmowers. The International Household Appliances Fair in Berlin gives us a glimpse into what's next.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany: Why is the AfD so popular in Saxony-Anhalt?
item.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to lead a state government since World War II. We discuss this with our guest, Hans Stark, professor of German studies at Sorbonne University.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau eruption halts flights, schools, fishing
item.description: An eruption of Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau caused six airports to suspend flight operations on Sunday, affecting hundreds of flights at Jakarta's main airport, after some school activities and fishing were halted.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Commemoration held for late Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic
item.description: A commemoration was held Saturday in Belgrade for war criminal Ratko Mladic two days ahead of his burial, attended by dozens of former military personnel, family members and officials.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
item.description: German voters headed to the polls on Sunday for a key regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigrant, Moscow- and Trump-friendly AfD is expected to secure an easy majority. Our correspondent Nick Holdsworth tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Ethan Hawke receives the Deauville Talent Award
item.description:
Known for starring in Dead Poets Society, the Before trilogy and Boyhood, Hollywood legend Ethan Hawke receives the #Deauville #Talent #Award in recognition of his career spanning nearly 40 years.
He also plays the lead role in The Weight, screened at the Opening Ceremony of the 52nd Deauville #American #Film #Festival and due to be released in theaters on September 16. Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca spoke to him on the red carpet.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll quits: "What we've seen is almost a factional clash"
item.description: Amid the US conflict with Iran, Democrats and some Republicans are warning of a leadership void at the top of the US military. That's after the resignation this week of the Army's top civilian official, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, amid widespread reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Our guest, Walter Ladwig, associate professor of international relations at King's College London, tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Trump's envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after 'substantive' talks with Putin
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Iran claims strike on US ship in Strait of Hormuz as fighting escalates
item.description: Iran said Sunday it struck an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz, the latest salvo in a new flare-up of fighting between the two countries.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nepal floods: Search operations enter 12th day
item.description:
Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations following catastrophic floods entered their 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescue of four survivors.
The disaster has also affected infrastructure and roads. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Germany's AfD chases historic breakthrough as Saxony-Anhalt votes
item.description: German voters headed to the polls Sunday for a crucial regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigration and Moscow-friendly AfD is expected to win easily.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon after alleged Hezbollah drone launch
item.description: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon Sunday killed four people, two of them women, the country's health ministry said. Israel's military said that the strikes were a response to an alleged Hezbollah drone launch targeting troops in the Israeli-occupied "security zone" in the country's south.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24
